features.title: Events
features.intro: IKY lets you host your own events — a wedding anniversary, a reunion, a housewarming — and invite people straight from your family tree. Invitees get notified in-app and by email, can RSVP, and a host can grant a trusted invitee extra visibility into the event's private details.

topics.title: Find the Hosted tab
steps: Event hosting lives inside the existing **Events** screen, alongside the **Dates** tab (birthdays, anniversaries, and remembrance days pulled automatically from your family tree). A new **Hosted** tab sits next to it.
Open **Events** from the bottom navigation, then tap **Hosted**.
Inside the Hosted tab there's a second-level switch: **Hosting** and **Invited**.
**Hosting** lists events you created — this is where you manage them.
**Invited** lists events other people have invited you to.
Each event in the list shows its date, title, and location (or its event type, if no location was set).

topics.title: Create an event
steps: While on the **Hosting** view, tap the **+** floating action button to open the **Create Event** form.
Fill in **Title** (required).
Optionally pick an **Event type** from a list (Marriage, House Warming, Family Reunion, Temple Visit, and more).
Set a **Start date** (required) and, for multi-day events, an optional **End date**.
Optionally add a **Location** and a short **Description**.
Tap **Create Event**. You'll see a confirmation ("Event created") and land back on the Hosting list with your new event at the top.

topics.title: Invite people
steps: Open an event you host from the Hosting list to reach its detail screen.
As the host, you'll see an **Invitees** section with an **Invite people** button.
Tap **Invite people** to open the invite screen, which uses the same member picker used elsewhere in the app to select people from your family tree.
Tap each person you want to invite — the button at the bottom updates to show how many you've selected (**Invite (N)**).
Tap **Invite (N)** to send the invites. Each invited person gets an in-app notification and an email, and the event now appears under their **Invited** view.

topics.title: Manage invitees and RSVPs
steps: Back on the event detail screen, the **Invitees** section lists everyone you've invited.
Each row shows the invitee (by email or person), their RSVP status — **Invited**, **Accepted**, or **Declined** — and a **Can manage** switch.

topics.title: What "Can manage" does
steps: By default, invitees only see the event's public details (title, type, dates, location, description).

If you add private host details to an event (for example, gate codes or a dress code only confirmed guests should see), those stay hidden from invitees — unless you flip their **Can manage** switch on.
An invitee with `can_manage` turned on can see those host-only details, the same way the host can.
Toggle **Can manage** on any invitee row at any time; it takes effect immediately.

topics.title: What an invitee sees
steps: When someone you invited opens the event (from their **Invited** view, their notification, or the email), they see the same event header — title, type, dates, location, description — plus their own response controls.
If they haven't responded yet, two buttons: **Decline** and **Accept**.
Once they've responded, their status is shown ("Your response: Accepted" or "Your response: Declined") with a link to switch their answer ("Accept instead" / "Decline instead").

The host sees the updated RSVP badge (**Invited** → **Accepted**/**Declined**) the next time they open the event or pull to refresh — responding doesn't push a live update to the host's screen while it's open.

topics.title: Notifications and email
steps: Every invite and RSVP change keeps both sides in the loop automatically.
**Inviting someone** sends them an in-app notification and an email with the event details.

**Responding to an invite** (Accept/Decline) does not notify the host — it updates the invitee's own status immediately, and the host sees the new RSVP badge the next time they open the event or pull to refresh.
No extra setup is needed on either side — notifications and email are sent automatically as part of the invite/RSVP actions above.
